result.title: WeightLoop: Weight-Space Programming with Experimental Feedback
result.summary: Weight-space programming (WSP) shows that language models can reason about and rewrite neural network weights; recursive self-improvement (RSI) motivates feedback-driven improvement. Models guiding experiments receive concrete feedback: completed assays reveal prediction errors and inform what to test next. We introduce WeightLoop, a framework that turns experimental feedback into persistent updates to deployed predictors. GPT-6 Astra inspects a task specification and the model implementation, then writes a bounded, reusable parameter-editing program. As new measurements arrive, the program identifies prediction discrepancies, validates candidate edits using observed outcomes, and writes the selected changes back to the original model. The editor remains fixed while the predictor evolves, enabling repeated updates without further LLM calls or gradient retraining while preserving the original inference interface. In offline replay, targeted edits improve mean ranking utility in seven of eight endpoint-budget settings (all eight versus random edits) and mean final discovery across three sequential tasks. WeightLoop connects WSP with an RSI-inspired improvement loop, making experimental evidence a direct driver of model change and subsequent decisions.

AI.brief_summary: WeightLoop 让 LLM 为任务模型编写有界、可复用的参数编辑程序，并利用新实验测量定位预测偏差、以观测结果验证候选权重修改后写回原模型，形成无需梯度重训的持续更新闭环。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用外部观测验证候选修改并决定是否写回」的机制，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、latent 状态更新的验证与信用分配提供类比；但论文不涉及视觉或 latent 推理，迁移可行性需核查。
